programme: REST/NRSF-mediated silencing of the neuronal differentiation gene battery — BDNF, GRIN2B, TAC1, VIP, GRIA2, SYP, TUBB3, NTRK3, TH, TPH2, CARTPT, MAPK8IP1 — the canonical REST target set, with REST itself observed bound at 7 of its own 25 listed targets by ReMap
role_in_a: In Huntington's disease, mutant huntingtin loses its normal cytoplasmic sequestration of REST, so REST accumulates in the nucleus and represses the neuronal gene battery it normally keeps active in post-mitotic neurons — most notably BDNF, but also GRIN2B, TAC1, VIP and other targets on this list — producing the transcriptional shutdown of neuronal identity genes seen in striatal and cortical HD tissue.
role_in_b: In lower-grade glioma, REST is co-opted as part of the dedifferentiation/stem-like programme: by silencing the same neuronal maturation genes (synaptic, neurotransmitter and cytoskeletal targets such as SYP, TUBB3, GRIA2) it helps hold tumour cells in a progenitor-like state, with reported REST regulatory-network differences between IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype glioma reflecting how strongly this repression is engaged.
shared_axis: Both diseases run the same REST-controlled neuronal gene battery in opposite directions of the same switch — HD via loss of upstream sequestration causing pathological nuclear REST activity, glioma via oncogenic maintenance of a progenitor-like REST-high state — so overlapping REST target sets between the two disease networks reflect the fact that REST governs one fixed set of neuronal genes regardless of which disease is driving its activity.
reasoning: REST is far and away the best-supported factor in the pair (286/651, roughly 12% above the next factor), sits at the 98th percentile of Open Targets HD associations, and is independently placed in each disease by a dedicated retrieved paper (midcingulate cortex expression disruption in HD; REST regulatory networks in IDH-mutant/wildtype glioma). The module — REST plus its own listed target genes — is nameable directly from the factor's target list without needing outside knowledge, which is what keeps this above 'moderate' despite no paper stating the HD-glioma link directly.
support: PMID 42080424 — REST-associated developmental gene expression disruption in Huntington's disease midcingulate cortex, placing REST activity directly in HD brain tissue; PMID 38711090 — REST transcription factor regulatory networks characterized separately in IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype lower-grade glioma, placing REST activity directly in glioma tumour biology.
how_to_falsify: Perform REST ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN in matched HD brain tissue and LGG tumour tissue and check whether the same target subset (BDNF, GRIN2B, TAC1, GRIA2, SYP, TUBB3) is bound and repressed concordantly in both; if REST occupies and represses a largely non-overlapping target set between the two tissues, or if REST protein is not detectably nuclear/active in the LGG samples used for this network, the shared-programme account fails.
caveats: Only REST is carried into this account; the other eleven concordant factors (PRRX1, ZFPM2, SP100, HEY2, HEYL, SMAD7, MEOX1, POU2AF1, SOX5, HDGF, IRF6) span unrelated programmes — TGF-beta/SMAD feedback, Notch-driven cardiovascular/smooth-muscle genes (HEY2/HEYL target sets are dominated by MYOCD, ACTA2, KDR, MYL2/7, not neuronal genes), B-cell coactivation (POU2AF1), PML/interferon body genes (SP100), craniofacial/innate-immune genes (IRF6) — and mostly lack disease-specific literature or Open Targets support in this record, so they were not forced into the story. SMAD7 has two glioma-specific papers but a near-zero HD percentile (0.04), so it looks glioma-only rather than shared, and was excluded rather than stretched to fit. HDGF has HD-specific support (PMID 37580082) but nothing for glioma, also excluded. The tissue pairing is blood|brain: HD network comparisons likely draw heavily on peripheral blood cohorts while the supporting HD paper for REST is brain (midcingulate cortex) tissue directly — the two need not track identically, so REST's blood-derived concordance score and its brain-tissue literature support should not be treated as the same measurement. 651 patient-group comparisons across only 4 independent cohort pairs means the denominator is inflated by repeated stratifications of few underlying cohorts, so the 286/651 figure overstates independent replication. The single-view exclusions (HOXD1, ZBTB20, PLAGL1, etc.) and tissue-generic exclusions (TCF4, EBF1, ETS1, STAT4, GLI1, LEF1, etc.) confirm that no classic blood-immune or generic-brain master regulator is being smuggled into this account — their absence here is by design, not an oversight.
